title: Sort Out the Three Conversations
coreMove: Separate a recent hard exchange into its facts, feelings, and identity layers before choosing any response.
sourcePressure: The chapter is a diagnostic entry point: every difficult exchange contains the what-happened, feelings, and identity conversations, with identity often least visible and most powerful.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating the three conversations as a tidy checklist or as the solution itself.

sourceAnchors.name: the three conversations
sourceAnchors.detail: The source names the what-happened, feelings, and identity conversations as simultaneous layers, with identity often quietest and most powerful.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Before you plan the perfect sentence, ask which of the three conversations is already running under it.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.

hook: Do not open ch01 with a generic dread-before-meeting frame
Do not begin with a definition of the chapter term
Do not use a negotiation-table abstraction as the first image
counterintuition: Avoid the shell 'you think X, but actually Y'
Avoid claiming the idea is simply counterintuitive
Avoid treating compassion as the surprising twist
tryThisNow: No 'pause and reflect on your communication style' action
examples: Avoid repeated coffee-table, classroom, narrow-kitchen, bus-depot, marker, mug, or radiator shells
Avoid six workplace meetings with changed names
Avoid making every case a manager feedback scene

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: use these six opening devices in order: sensory detail first; dialogue first line; timestamp+name+action; second-person You direct address; retrospective first line; environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of timestamp plus named protagonist plus prop plus decision that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.audience: new managers giving feedback to veteran staff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a missed medication-reconciliation deadline could become a patient-safety issue
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager puts the printed deadline log beside a blank page labeled feelings and identity, then writes her own identity fear before drafting the first sentence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a stapled incident log under fluorescent light
mustAvoid: generic office feedback with no identity stakes

exampleSpecs.audience: readers handling family logistics that carry old roles
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next weekend visit to their father is still unassigned after 47 texts
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one sibling stops answering the logistics thread and circles the three separate layers on a notepad before calling
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone screen still glowing on a kitchen counter

exampleSpecs.domain: software co-founders debating a vendor renewal
exampleSpecs.audience: founders and partners whose data argument is stuck
exampleSpecs.stakes: the renewal deadline is Friday and trust between partners is eroding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the founder points to the same spreadsheet and then says the contract is not the only conversation in the room
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a shared spreadsheet projected in a quiet conference room

exampleSpecs.domain: tenant association meeting about elevator outages
exampleSpecs.audience: neighbors in civic conflict with layered stakes
exampleSpecs.stakes: elderly residents feel trapped and the board fears being branded negligent
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you watch the board chair sort complaint dates, fear, and competence onto three separate sticky-note columns
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three columns of sticky notes on a folding table

exampleSpecs.audience: graduate students facing credit and identity pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: a poster submission deadline forces unresolved contribution questions into the open
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes the student three weeks to see that the authorship fight is also about belonging in the field
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a half-finished poster on a shared lab drive

exampleSpecs.stakes: a singer believes the director's choice says something about her place in the group
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director names facts, hurt, and identity privately before replying to the singer's email
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sheet music stacked on a piano bench

skillTargets: identify when a scenario needs separate a recent hard exchange into its facts, feelings, and identity layers before choosing any response.
distinguish three conversations from the adjacent generic misread
choose the visible action that demonstrates the chapter move rather than merely naming it
explain why the wrong option would recreate treating the three conversations as a tidy checklist or as the solution itself.

tryThisNowSpec: Take one avoided conversation and write three labels: what happened, feelings, identity. Put one concrete stake under each label before planning any words.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
